plain_description.what: On a six-dataset combined pool, sends each held-out question to its nearest tree leaf and answers it with the model that did best on that leaf's training questions. Accuracy is compared with routing by the designed dataset/domain groups.
plain_description.why: It asks whether the discovered fine-grained taxonomy routes questions to models better than the obvious human-designed categories.
plain_description.information: It shows whether fine leaves add routing value or spread the data too thin. Result: done. As first read, the grown tree lost to the designed domains (59.2% vs 60.1%, -0.9 points), as predicted, which suggested that model strengths sit at family or domain level and that leaves dilute support. A later clean re-read on the split of record gives -0.09 points with an interval from -1.1 to +0.9, descriptive only, so the loss is not reproduced as a decided result. An open flag remains: the held-out side may overlap with training content and has not been re-verified (pool checked by id only).
